title: Preserve the paid global-tree operation and disprove a marginal-to-uniform-law shortcut
statement: At the supplied2610.10898v1 contract, given an OUT-arborescence T and q dominating SOME feasible arborescence point, one global demand flow on O(m log^2 n) edges plus expectation-preserving integral rounding/two-tree partition yields E[1_Tprime|T]<=(1_T+q)/2. The dominance hypothesis and actual flow costs are paid; its integer-weight mincut application is not a nearlinear BIT uniform sampler, and flow projection h itself need not be a fractional arborescence. Root gives an exact law obstruction on bidirected K4 rooted at r: uniform four inward stars and uniform twelve inward Hamiltonian paths both have marginals P(u->r)=1/2 and P(u->v)=1/4 for distinct nonroots, by adjacency/symmetry, yet disjoint supports give TV=1. Thus contracting/preserving arc marginals alone does not establish the required joint uniform tree/tour law. This is not a no-go for a fuller global-update sampler.
